html:
The third of the three great tragic poets of Athens, born around 480 BCE. Later legend said he was born on the day of the Battle of Salamis.

He wrote around 90 plays, and more of them survive than of Aeschylus and Sophocles together: eighteen or nineteen, depending on how one is counted. Among them are:

  • Medea (431 BCE), about a woman who kills her children to punish her unfaithful husband
  • The Trojan Women (415 BCE), about the suffering of captives after a war
  • The Bacchae, about the god Dionysus' terrible revenge

His plays give strong roles to women, slaves and outsiders, and question the justice of the gods. He won only a few first prizes in his life, and Aristophanes mocked him on stage. He spent his last years at the court of the king of Macedon and died there in 406 BCE.

He became the most popular of the three after his death. Plutarch says some Athenians captured in the Sicilian Expedition won their freedom by reciting his verses.
sum: The third of the three great tragic poets of Athens, born around 480 BCE. Later legend said he was born on the day of the Battle of Salamis.
